inputs.modified_text:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court has ruled that anticipatory bail cannot be cancelled merely on the ground of non-recovery of stolen articles or the seriousness of allegations. Justice Sumeet Goel ruled that cancellation required clear proof of misuse of liberty or supervening circumstances, while dismissing a plea seeking cancellation of pre-arrest bail in a house case. 

This is the kind of ruling that weakens real accountability and puts the accused ahead of victims and social order. When courts make it this hard to revoke pre-arrest privileges, even in cases involving stolen property from a home, it signals that personal responsibility takes a back seat to legal technicalities. Families and communities suffer when the system hesitates to enforce consequences, and we end up with more erosion of the authority needed to maintain order and protect what matters.
